# Scientific fixture expectations

All JEOL fixture decodes and Bruker NUS fixtures explicitly opt into
experimental vendor semantics. Default entry points must reject those paths;
synthetic success does not lift the independent-evidence restriction. The
Bruker DSPFVS/DECIM group-delay table is tested by `tests/reading/bruker/group_delay.rs`.

These files are minimal byte fixtures. Tests have no external data dependency.
Accepted-layout fixtures exercise the layouts implemented by the readers.
Fixtures freeze supported decoding behavior; they do not independently authorize
a format interpretation. The table below links to the public
[format-rule source register](../../docs/src/content/docs/scientific-contract.md#format-rule-sources).
Its external references and explicit evidence gaps take precedence over historical
`PrimarySource`, `ExpertConfirmed`, or `CorroboratedOracle` fixture labels.

All repository fixtures and the synthetic processed fixtures generated by
`tests/reading/` are original test data distributed under the repository's
`MIT OR Apache-2.0` license. The generated fixtures are written only below a
per-test temporary directory; they do not depend on sibling applications,
absolute paths, or external implementations.

`jcamp_dx/scaled-dif.dx` is a fixed conformance fixture with an inline producer
comment, `XFACTOR=0.1`, multiline DIF checkpoints, and the required terminal
`END` record. Its actual X coordinates are `100, 101, 102, 103` Hz and its
decoded ordinates are exactly `10, 11, 12, 13`.

## Fixture organization

Vendor inputs are grouped in `bruker/`, `jeol/`, `varian/` and `jcamp_dx/`.
Frozen NPZ output lives in `npz/`.
Names describe the format and layout; an experimental reader option can still
be required for a fixture whose filename does not say "rejected".

Additional reading regression inputs are constructed from explicit scalar values
and standard parameter fields, with generic synthetic titles. They contain no
experimental or personal data, are distributed under MIT OR Apache-2.0, and
establish regression behavior rather than independent vendor correctness:

| Input | Construction and expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `jcamp_dx/ppm.dx` | JCAMP 5.00 baseline; tests change only the declaration to 5.01. Coordinates are 4,3,2,1 ppm; scaled samples are 2,4,6,8. |
| `bruker/nus-2d/` | FnTYPE=2, FnMODE=6; grid 4; observations 3,1; two indirect lanes. Tests omit `nuslist`, supply an explicit one-based declaration 4,2, then compare with the companion-file import. |
| `bruker/processed-1d/pdata/1/` | SF=400 without an acquisition file; samples 2,4,6,8 at 10,7.5,5,2.5 ppm. Reference is known; observe frequency and filter correction are unknown. |

## Generated processed fixtures

| Format | Generator and field evidence | Expected bits and order |
|---|---|---|
| Bruker TopSpin 1D | `processed_parameters`; `SI=3`, `DTYPP=0`, `BYTORDP=0`, `NC_proc=1`; `1r` int32 LE | scalar direct-fastest `2.0, -4.0, 6.0` |
| Bruker TopSpin 2D | `SI=XDIM=2` on both axes; `2rr` int32 LE | `[F1,F2]`, F2 direct-fastest `2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0` |
| JCAMP-DX 5.00 | fixed `scaled-dif.dx` plus generated AFFN/ASDF cases; Hz, scaled checkpoints and inline comments | scalar source order; fixed DIF fixture decodes `10.0, 11.0, 12.0, 13.0` |
| JEOL Delta processed | JDF v1, dimension 1, axis type `[3]`, Hz unit, float64 LE, valid window `1..=2` | public `R+iI`, interleaved `2.0, -20.0, 3.0, -30.0` |

The assertions compare exact `f64` values; integral source values and power-of-two
scales make their IEEE-754 bit patterns exact. Compression tests additionally
cover JCAMP AFFN, PACKED, SQZ, DIF, DUP, DIFDUP, multiline X/Y checkpoints,
inline comments, and block termination.

## Layout evidence

| Fixture | Expected contract | Source register entry / limitation |
|---|---|---|
| `bruker/one-dimensional.fid` | 1D complex int32, `R + iI` | `bruker.direct.v1`: nmrglue v0.11 storage implementation |
| `bruker/two-dimensional-kblock.ser` | dense States-TPPI, 1024-byte rows | Bruker revision 007 modes; nmrglue v0.11 row boundaries; parity regression |
| `bruker/two-dimensional-contiguous.ser` | dense echo/anti-echo, contiguous rows | Bruker revision 007 `xfb`; analytic component regression |
| `jeol/axis-1.jdf` | `[1]`, real direct axis | `jeol.direct.v1`: independent source coverage incomplete |
| `jeol/axis-3.jdf` | `[3]`, complex direct axis with explicit imaginary sign transform | `jeol.direct.v1`: independent source coverage incomplete |
| `jeol/axes-3-1.jdf` | `[3,1]`, 2D tile reorder and crop | JEOL accepted-layout regression; independent source coverage incomplete |
| `jeol/axes-3-3.jdf` | `[3,3]`, lanes `S0-i*S1`, `-S2+i*S3` | `jeol.cartesian-2d.v1`: nmrglue 0.12 signs and analytic processing |
| `jeol/axes-4-4.jdf` | `[4,4]`, one pair shared with opposite F1 orientation | `jeol.shared-complex-2d.v1`: signed tones and real COSY audit |
| `varian/complex.fid` | complex status, block scale, stored real/quadrature lanes | Fixed OpenVnmrJ headers/storage source; direct-sign derivation |
| `varian/real.fid` | real status; even `np` does not imply complex | Fixed OpenVnmrJ `data.h` status bits |
| `varian/eight-trace.fid` | trace-order and NUS coordinate mapping input | Library mapping regression; not independent acquisition evidence |
| `varian/two-block.fid` | per-block storage scaling and block order | Fixed OpenVnmrJ headers/storage source |
| `npz/plot-v1.npz` | complete deterministic NPZ V1 archive | Library serialization regression |

The Varian fixtures are synthetic, so they do not independently establish a
physical direct-axis Fourier direction. The public source register traces the
sign derivation to OpenVnmrJ commit
`5e20f6f77dd5331473e47402153cb9dd310eb3d4`. The synthetic tone regression
freezes the reader-to-FFT contract without redistributing real acquisitions.

## Sample-bit projections

All sample assertions compare `f64::to_bits()` for both public complex lanes.

| Fixture/projection | Expected public samples |
|---|---|
| Bruker 1D | `(10,-20), (30,-40)` |
| Bruker 2D trace `[1]`, every indirect lane | `(21,22), (23,24), (31,32), (33,34)` |
| Bruker incomplete NUS trace `[3]` | `(1,2), (3,4), (11,12), (13,14)` |
| Bruker complete NUS trace `[1]` | `(1,2), (3,4), (11,12), (13,14)` |
| JEOL `[1]` | `(1,0), (2,0), (3,0), (4,0)` |
| JEOL `[3]` | `(1,-10), (2,-20), (3,-30), (4,-40)` |
| JEOL `[3,1]` trace `[2]` | `(20,-1020)` through `(25,-1025)` |
| Varian complex | `(2,-4), (6,-8)` |
| Varian real | `(2,0), (4,0), (6,0), (8,0)` |
| Varian Regular trace `[1,0]` | `(4,4), (5,5), (6,6), (7,7)` |
| Varian Opposite trace `[1,0]` | `(4,4), (6,6), (5,5), (7,7)` |
| Varian complete NUS trace `[5]` | `(2,2)` |
| Varian incomplete NUS trace `[7]` | `(0,0)` |
| Varian two-block trace `[1]` | `(20,-24), (28,-32)` |

## Error scenarios

| Mutation or request | Expected kind | Required structured reason |
|---|---|---|
| JEOL byte length below every header boundary | `Truncated` | `Truncated { expected, actual, input }` |
| Unsupported JEOL axis-type vector | `UnsupportedFeature` | `UnsupportedFeature { input, code, axis, evidence }` |
| Varian layout outside the v1 truth table | `UnsupportedFeature` | `VARIAN_UNSUPPORTED_COMPONENT_LAYOUT` |
| Varian missing block header | `Corrupt` | `Corrupt { input, detail }` |
| Varian exact binary length mismatch | `Truncated` or `Corrupt` | source-specific reason, never panic |
| Bruker missing parameter | `InvalidMetadata` | `InvalidMetadata` with typed `ParameterError` source |
| Bruker malformed/duplicate/invalid parameter | `InvalidMetadata` | structured `ParameterError` |
| Sparse absent trace | `UnsampledCoordinate` | `Access(UnsampledCoordinate)` |
| Sparse empty region | `UnsampledRegion` | `Access(UnsampledRegion)` |
| Region byte cap | `LimitExceeded` | `RegionBytes` |
| Dense materialization byte cap | `LimitExceeded` | `MaterializedBytes` |

Complete and incomplete NUS tests assert schedule order exactly as stored by the
normalized model. Eager/lazy parity tests assert nonzero logical coordinates and all
component lanes independently of these fixture tables.
